findings.key_quote: On November 18, 2024, the European Commission issued a decision that Meta infringed Article 102 on the Treaty of the Functioning of the European Union in relation to certain alleged business practices relating to Facebook Marketplace and imposed a fine of approximately EUR € 798 million. We appealed the European Commission's decision on January 28, 2025. In March 2024, the European Commission opened an investigation into the compliance of our "subscription for no ads" consent model with requirements under Article 5(2) of the Digital Markets Act (DMA). The European Commission issued preliminary findings on July 1, 2024 reflecting its preliminary view that our model does not comply with such requirements. In April 2025, the European Commission issued a final decision that our "subscription for no ads" model does not comply with such requirements and imposed a fine of EUR € 200 million.
findings.justification: This evidence from the 10-Q filed 2026-04-30 for period ending 2026-03-31 (EXACT_MATCH) discloses two substantial EU fines totaling approximately EUR €998 million (€798 million + €200 million). These are material financial exposures in the European Union that were disclosed as of March 31, 2026. The assertion claims no material financial exposure, but these fines represent significant disclosed liabilities, directly contradicting the claim.

findings.key_quote: In April 2025, the European Commission issued a final decision that our "subscription for no ads" model does not comply with such requirements and imposed a fine of EUR € 200 million.
findings.justification: This evidence from the 10-Q filed 2026-04-30 for period ending 2026-03-31 (EXACT_MATCH) discloses a EUR €200 million fine imposed by the European Commission. This is a material financial exposure in the European Union disclosed as of March 31, 2026, contradicting the assertion that there is no material financial exposure.

findings.key_quote: We believe that the amount of losses or any estimable range of possible losses with respect to these other matters will not, either individually or in the aggregate, have a material adverse effect on our business and condensed consolidated financial statements.
findings.justification: This evidence from the 10-Q filed 2026-04-30 for period ending 2026-03-31 (EXACT_MATCH) states management's belief about 'other matters' not having a material adverse effect. However, this statement refers to matters beyond the specifically disclosed EU fines (Facebook Marketplace €798M and DMA €200M), which are separately disclosed and not covered by this general statement. This is context about other matters but does not decide whether the specifically disclosed EU regulatory matters represent material exposure.
